newsitem.title: USA: Troy, N.Y. to vote on $36 mln budget in Dec--paper.
newsitem.headline: Troy, N.Y. to vote on $36 mln budget in Dec--paper.

text.p: The City Council of Troy, N.Y., which recently reached a last-minute refinancing pact, is expected to vote in December on an approximately $36 million budget, the Albany Times Union said Wednesday.
The paper said the budget proposed by Mayor Mark Pattison is about $200,000 smaller than this year's $36 million general fund, and about $5 million less than the 1995 budget.
While the council in 1996 approved a mid-year tax hike of 21 percent due to the city's financial problems, the new budget calls for the tax rate to remain the same.
The proposed budget includes $1 million more in healthcare costs.

Firefighters will get 2.25 percent increases while police command officers will obtain four percent raises that were delayed from 1995. No other employees will see their pay increase, the paper quoted the mayor as saying.
Concessions made by the firefighters will let the city spend $500,000 less than budgeted for in 1996, and $1.3 million less than in 1995.

Rising revenues are projected for the fire department's ambulence service, which is expected to produce $550,000, up from the $360,000 estimated for this year. And the new budget forecasts collections of traffic fines will climb to $245,000 from $162,000.
The mayor's budget includes $1 million from a federal program, the Community Block Development Grant, up from $675,000.
But no further rises in state aid are anticipated, though the paper said Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, has said he will try to make a $2.8 million jump in state aid recurring.
